title: Merge overlapping ranges
prompt: Each interval is a pair [start, end] with start no greater than end. Return the intervals merged so that none overlap or touch: [1, 3] and [2, 6] become [1, 6], and [1, 2] and [2, 3] become [1, 3]. The result is sorted by start. The input may be in any order, and must not be changed.
hints: In what order would every interval that overlaps the current one come right after it?
Sort a copy by start. Then keep the last merged interval, and compare each next interval's start with its end.
If the next start is no greater than the last end, extend the last end to the larger of the two ends. Otherwise push a new pair.
checkLabels: 1 to 3 and 2 to 6 merge. 8 to 10 stays apart.
No intervals give an empty array.
The input may be in any order.
An interval inside another does not shorten it.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Assumes the intervals arrive sorted by start.
Takes the end of the newest interval, even when the earlier one ends later.

feedback: Draw the intervals on a number line. Once they are sorted by start, each one either extends the range you are building or begins a new one.
